title: Embodied First Exam: An Agentic Robotics Benchmark
summary: Coding agents have passed many exams in the digital world. What is their first exam before entering the physical world? What the exam is, how ten coding agents do on its core set in three settings, and four findings on where they fail.

title: Where Do Today’s Agentic Robots Succeed and Fail?
summary: Towards understanding the capability boundary of coding agents in robotics: which tasks each of ten agents fails and why, what information matters, where in a task they fail, and what changes the result.

title: Embodied Olympics: Can Agentic Robots Continually Improve Through Competition?
summary: Coding agents as robotics engineers: in 18 simulated sports, seven agents build, run and revise the systems that control robots. They build a strong first system, but the loop of noticing a failure, changing the program and checking the change rarely makes the robot better.

title: GPT-6.2 Astra
summary: GPT-6.2 Astra solves the most tests of the Embodied First Exam in the Privileged and Standard Settings. Where it gains on Claude Fable 5.2, what an attempt costs, where it fails while other agents succeed, and runs side by side.
